Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: In a choir, the ratio of sopranos to altos is two to three, and the ratio of altos to tenors is four to five. There are thirty tenors. How many singers are in the choir?
We have two ratios, and one group, the altos, appears in both. That's the key. We'll solve it two ways, the math way with one shared number, and then the math way starting from the tenors.
Let's start with the math way. Here are the two ratios. Sopranos to altos is two to three, and altos to tenors is four to five.
at: Sopranos to altos is two to three
altos to tenors is four to five

slides.say: Many students glue them together and write two to three to five. That gives sixty, choice number two, and it's wrong. Why? Both ratios describe the same altos, but use different unit sizes. Three and four aren't the same, so we can't join the ratios yet.
at: Both ratios describe the same altos

slides.say: Let's see the idea on easy numbers first. If A to B is one to two, and B to C is two to three, then B is two in both ratios. So we can write A to B to C as one to two to three.
at: If A to B is one to two
So we can write A to B to C

slides.say: In our question, the altos are three in one ratio and four in the other. So we need one number that both three and four go into. Three times four is twelve.

Sopranos to altos is two to three. To turn the three into twelve, we multiply by four. We multiply both numbers, so the ratio stays the same. Two times four is eight. Three times four is twelve. So the ratio is eight to twelve.
Altos to tenors is four to five. To turn the four into twelve, we multiply by three. Four times three is twelve. Five times three is fifteen. So the ratio is twelve to fifteen.
Now the altos are twelve in both ratios, so we can join them. Sopranos to altos to tenors is eight to twelve to fifteen.
Now the real number. There are thirty tenors, and the tenors are fifteen x. Fifteen x is thirty, so x is two.

The whole choir is eight x plus twelve x plus fifteen x. Eight plus twelve is twenty. Twenty plus fifteen is thirty-five. So that's thirty-five x. Thirty-five times two is seventy singers. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now a second way. We start again from the givens, and this time from the real number. There are thirty tenors.
Altos to tenors is four to five, four altos for every five tenors. So the altos are four fifths of the tenors. A fifth of thirty is six, and four fifths is four times six, twenty-four altos.
at: So the altos are four fifths

slides.say: Sopranos to altos is two to three. So the sopranos are two thirds of the altos. A third of twenty-four is eight, and two thirds is sixteen sopranos.
at: So the sopranos are two thirds
A third of twenty-four is eight

slides.say: Altogether, sixteen plus twenty-four is forty. Then forty plus thirty is seventy. We get the same seventy.

So when two ratios share a group, first make that group the same number in both ratios. Then you can join them into one ratio. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
